items.title: CVE-2026-119586 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite command-line shell through 3.54.1 contains a command injection vulnerability in the .recover command that emits attacker-planted dot-commands stored in sqlite_schema.sql values verbatim. Attackers can craft a database whose schema holds a valid CREATE statement followed by a .shell or .system line, executing OS commands when victims pipe .recover output into sqlite3.
items.summary: SQLite up to 3.54.1 is vulnerable to command injection via the .recover command, affecting applications parsing untrusted databases. No fix yet: watch for a patch.
items.holdReason: Requires opening an attacker-crafted database file.

items.title: CVE-2026-119591 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability in countOfViewOptimization() that allows attackers to crash the host process via count(*) over a large multi-row VALUES clause. Attackers supplying SQL or a database file with a crafted view can trigger deeply nested TK_PLUS expressions whose recursive freeing in sqlite3ExprDeleteNN() exhausts the C stack, causing denial of service.
items.summary: SQLite before 3.54.0 has a stack exhaustion vulnerability in countOfViewOptimization() that can crash the host process via crafted views, affecting applications processing untrusted databases. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119371 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH nesting limit because common table expressions are not counted against it. Attackers can supply a WITH clause chaining tens of thousands of CTEs, via plain SQL or a view in an untrusted database file, causing unbounded selectExpander() recursion that crashes the process.
items.summary: SQLite contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability via common table expressions that affects applications processing untrusted SQL. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119372 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS3/FTS4 and SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3_PARENTHESIS contains a use-after-free vulnerability in fts3BestSnippet() caused by dangling cached position-list pointers. Attackers can run a full-text MATCH query combining OR and NEAR operators with snippet() to read freed heap memory and crash the process.
items.summary: SQLite built with FTS3/FTS4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability via full-text MATCH queries that affects applications processing crafted search input. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119373 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap buffer overflow in fts5MergeRowidLists() that undersizes the output buffer when merging detail=none prefix doclists. Attackers who can populate a detail=none FTS5 table with negative rowids and run a prefix MATCH query can write past the allocation, corrupting heap memory and crashing the process.
items.summary: SQLite built with FTS5 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability via prefix MATCH queries that affects applications processing untrusted full-text search data. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119374 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap buffer overflow in fts5DoSecureDelete() that allows attackers to write past the leaf page buffer via crafted footer key offsets. Attackers can supply a database file with a corrupted FTS5 index that, when deleted from with secure-delete enabled, corrupts heap memory and crashes the application.
items.summary: SQLite built with FTS5 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in secure-delete operations that affects applications handling corrupted database indices. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119375 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to read uninitialized page-cache memory by supplying a WAL file with an undersized page size. Attackers can craft a database and WAL file whose oversized record payload makes queries like substr() return stale bytes, disclosing other table rows and internal pointers.
items.summary: SQLite contains an information disclosure vulnerability via WAL files that affects applications reading uninitialized page-cache memory. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119377 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in lookupName() that invokes the authorizer only for the first joined table's USING column. Attackers able to submit SQL can query a shared USING column in a RIGHT or FULL JOIN to read columns denied via sqlite3_set_authorizer() SQLITE_READ restrictions.
items.summary: SQLite contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in JOIN queries that affects applications relying on column-level authorizers. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119378 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the R-Tree extension that allows attackers to make applications use freed heap memory by manipulating the %_node shadow table. Attackers can supply a database declaring %_node WITHOUT ROWID or with a RAISE(IGNORE) trigger so nodeWrite() hashes nodes as 0, crashing the process after node splits.
items.summary: SQLite contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the R-Tree extension that affects applications manipulating shadow tables. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-119379 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 built with the session extension contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in sqlite3changeset_apply() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying crafted changesets. Attackers can repeat a table name in a second changeset block with a larger column count, causing sessionUpdateFind() to memset past the undersized aUpdateMask allocation.
items.summary: SQLite built with the session extension contains a heap buffer overflow via crafted changesets that affects applications applying database changes. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.snippet: Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well! Weight-Space Programming Here's the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights: Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about,…

items.summary: A remote code execution vulnerability exists in Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver versions prior to 2.3.0 due to unsafe class loading via connection parameters. Developers and systems using these driver versions are affected. Upgrade the Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver to 2.3.0 or later.
